activity.notes: Representative Canton merchant span begins with Howqua/Wu Bingjian inheriting the Yihe Company in 1801. The end uses his reported 1834 retirement as a conservative representative boundary; later influence continued, so end certainty is approximate rather than falsely exact.

sources.title: Uncovering the garden of the richest man on earth in nineteenth-century Canton: Howqua's garden in Honam, China
sources.citation_text: The University of Sheffield/White Rose paper identifies Howqua as Wu Bingjian (1769–1843) and states that he inherited the Yihe Company in 1801, after which it became highly profitable.
sources.locator: Howqua, richest man on earth in the first half of the nineteenth century

sources.title: Portrait of the Chinese Merchant Howqua (Wu Bingjian) — Christie’s
sources.citation_text: Christie's identifies Howqua as the wealthiest and most successful Co-Hong merchant and records his retirement in 1834 and death in 1843.

review_context.identity_note: Current canonical writer has no separate alias field; the historically essential alternate identity Wu Bingjian is retained in the canonical English display.
